text:
maria: Heads up — GraniteHealth private cutover canary is spiking latency and one canary instance failed TLS handshake. anyone on call?

ajay: saw alert at 12:12 PT. quick glance at logs shows TLS negotiation errors on the canary path.

ajay: logs snippet:
```
curl https://granite.internal/health -v
* Rebuilt URL to: https://granite.internal/health/
*   Trying 10.0.3.12...
* Connected to granite.internal (10.0.3.12) port 443 (#0)
*  TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
*  TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2):
*  SSL: certificate problem: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```

kevin: @ajay can you confirm whether this is our rotated CA or customer cert?

ajay: we rolled the interop CA last week. Canary should be using customer-provided cert (pinned), but error is "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" so looks like CA mismatch.

oliver: I opened PR to refresh CA bundle for private canaries (#4621) — pending review from @maria. If merged, new canaries will pick up the updated CA.

maria: @oliver i can review in ~30m. in the meantime can @kevin check LB and NAT behavior? GraniteOps reported retransmits.

kevin: checked network path, no packet drops on fabric. NAT timeouts look normal. I see TLS handshake packets reaching the LB, but backend is replying RST intermittently. could be SNI mismatch or an old canary image behind the LB.

ajay: SNI in our logs is 'granite-vpc.granite.local' — correct. slo-bot shows 2 canary instances: canary-a (image v2025.11, CA old) and canary-b (image v2026.02, CA refreshed). believed traffic split is 50/50.

maria: ok ownership: @oliver merge CA bundle PR and trigger canary rollout; @ajay will smoke-test after rollout; @kevin will tail LB logs and enable pcap capture for the window; i'll ping Granite ops for cert thumbprint and ask them to confirm they didn't rotate cert last night.

oliver: on it — merging in ~15m, will post deploy command and canary id.

ajay: after deploy i'll run smoke and paste results: `curl -v https://granite.internal/health` and attach logs.

GraniteOpsBot: Received webhook: GraniteOps will verify cert thumbprint and respond with confirmation within 1 hour.

maria: :thumbsup: updating runbook (private-cutover-runbook.md) to add this CA-check step and a rollback if canary fail rate > 5% for 10m.

kevin: i'll set up LB capture and alert if RST > 2% for TLS handshakes. will report back ASAP.

maria: thanks team — posting async updates here. if anyone finds a blocker, ping #oncall immediately.
